propositions: Plan-review grounding finders block plans that rely on symbols a depends_on prerequisite will create, treating those symbols as missing/unverifiable despite prose-level spec that they should be treated as existing.

The grounding logic checks only the origin/main snapshot and ignores the ticket's prerequisites, failing to honor the stated rule that symbols created by depended-upon tickets are treated as existing.

A machine-parseable inline citation grammar [rebar:<ticket-id>] with two-layer verification (deterministic advisory edge-check plus LLM coverage confirmation) can ground symbols in prerequisite tickets without adding a blocking check to the deterministic floor.

Layer-1 advisory verification must confirm a cited ticket is a direct upstream prerequisite via both-direction edge check: either the plan ticket declares depends_on(cited) or the cited ticket declares blocks(plan), with reverse-lookup error handling that treats failures as unverified (fail-closed).

Layer-2 LLM protocol must credit a symbol citation only if the cited ticket's plan/file_impact affirmatively establishes the specific functionality claimed missing, with explicit fail-closed behavior for uncited, edge-unbacked, or coverage-unconfirmed citations.
Behavioral evaluation confirms the protocol credits verified and covered citations while withholding credit for edge-unbacked or coverage-absent citations, preserving fail-closed semantics.
